diagnostic_evidence.quote: \bA_1 = L_1 \bA R_1^\top = P_1 \bar L_1 \bA \bar R_1^\top Q_1^\top = P_1 \bar{\bA}_1 Q_1^\top.
P_{t+1} \bar L_{t+1} P_t L_t \bA R_t^\top Q_t^\top \bar R_{t+1}^\top Q_{t+1}^\top

issues.failure_explanation: The base case and the conclusion have the form A_t = P_t Ā_t Q_t^T, i.e. Ā_t = P_t^T A_t Q_t. The induction step instead uses Σ Ā Ā^T = P_t(Σ A A^T)P_t^T and later P_t L_t A R_t^T Q_t^T = Ā_t, which both require Ā_t = P_t A_t Q_t^T. As written, the hypothesis assumed and the conclusion derived do not match, so the induction does not close. The statement also has R_0 = I_m (should be I_n), A_t = L_t A R_t (missing transpose), and an undefined L_0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Run the induction with P_t, Q_t replaced by P_t^T, Q_t^T in the step (i.e. use Ā_t = P_t^T A_t Q_t), giving L_{t+1} = P_{t+1} L̄_{t+1} P_t^T L_t, and similarly for R. Also fix R_0 = I_n, A_t = L_t A R_t^T and L_0 = I.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the equivalence of OSI and the factor fixed-point iteration (used to justify focusing on Algorithm 2) is not established. The claim itself remains true.
issues.title: Induction step in proof of algorithm equivalence uses the inverse of the induction hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A routine transposition bookkeeping fix closes the induction; the statement and its use are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: when $\omega > 1$ is used (which is the case of interest in overrelaxation) it cannot be guaranteed that positive definite matrices are generated.

issues.failure_explanation: For ω > 1, take X = cI with c large and any Y ∈ O. Then (1-ω)cI + ωS_1(Y) has negative eigenvalues, so S_ω does not map C_m × O into C_m × C_n. Well-definedness requires X to be near X_* as well; the second component also needs the new X near X_*. The subsequent 'Therefore' conclusion about a neighborhood of the orbit rests on this false premise.

failure_location.quote: is well defined as a map from $\caC_m \times \mathcal O$ to $\caC_m \times \caC_n$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace C_m × O by a neighborhood of (X_*,Y_*) in C_m × C_n, then extend to a neighborhood of the orbit via the equivariance (2.x).
issues.overall_effect: The stated domain of S_ω is wrong for the overrelaxation regime. Lemma equal derivatives only uses a neighborhood of (X_*,Y_*), so the formal results are unaffected.
issues.title: Euclidean SOR map claimed well defined on C_m × O for a neighborhood O of Y_* only
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the domain suffices; no result or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking the trace of Σ x̃_i x̃_i^T = I_n gives Σ||x̃_i||^2 = n. With ||x̃_i|| = n/k this would require n^2/k = n, so the stated problem is infeasible unless n = k; it is infeasible for the experiment's n = 50, k = 55. Moreover, with x̃_i = α_i R x_i and α_i = nℓ_i^2, one gets Σ x̃_i x̃_i^T = Σ n^2 ℓ_i^4 (Rx_i)(Rx_i)^T ≠ I_n in general. The correct choice is α_i = √n ℓ_i, giving ||x̃_i||^2 = n/k.

failure_location.quote: So $P = R$ and $\alpha_i = n\ell_i^2$ yield a solution to frame scaling, and vice versa.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the norm condition as ||x̃_i||_2^2 = n/k with positive α_i, and use α_i = √n ℓ_i (or x̃_i = √α_i P x_i with α_i = nℓ_i^2).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalence between frame scaling and the operator scaling instance used in the experiments is incorrect as stated.
issues.title: Frame scaling formulation infeasible and reduction formula incorrect
issues.why_classification: A short local correction of the formulation restores the equivalence; the experiments run on the operator scaling instance are unaffected.

Assume that the CP map $\Phi$ is positivity improving, and let $(X_*,Y_*)$ be a fixed-point

issues.failure_explanation: For A_i = e_i x_i^T, take w = e_1 and nonzero v ⟂ x_1 (possible since n = 50 > 1). Then w^T A_i v = 0 for all i, so Φ is not positivity improving. The positive-matrix Perron–Frobenius argument of Lemma null space and Theorem local convergence therefore do not apply. The prose nevertheless presents the experiment as validating the theorem and suggests the experiments satisfy the assumptions.

failure_location.quote: We see that the convergence rates of all three SOR methods are the same, validating the local convergence result in Theorem~\ref{thm: local convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the frame-scaling results as empirical behaviour outside the theorem's hypotheses, or prove a version of Lemma null space / Theorem local convergence under a weaker condition covering this instance.
issues.overall_effect: The experimental confirmation of Theorem local convergence is overstated: the observed equal rates lie outside the proven scope.
issues.title: Frame-scaling experiment claimed to validate local theorem whose hypothesis fails there
